title: Pointers

exercises.title: Declare a Pointer
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to an int named 'ptr' that points to a variable 'x' with value 42. Print the pointer value using printf(ptr).

exercises.title: Dereference a Pointer
exercises.description: Create a pointer to an int and use the * operator to access and print the value it points to.

exercises.title: Pass Pointer to Function
exercises.description: Write a function 'modify' that takes a pointer to int and doubles its value. Call it with a variable and print the result.

exercises.title: Use the new Keyword
exercises.description: Use the 'new' keyword to allocate a new int pointer, assign a value to it, and print the dereferenced value.

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string). Create a pointer to Person using & and set Name to "Bob". Print Name through the pointer.
hints: `struct Person p = {"Bob"}; puts(p.name);` — or `struct Person *p = &person; puts(p->name);`

exercises.title: Nil Pointer Check
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to int named ptr without initializing it. Check if it is nil and print "nil" or the dereferenced value.
hints: `if (ptr == NULL) puts("nil");` — with `ptr` initialized `NULL`, you always print `nil` here.

exercises.title: Swap with Pointers
exercises.description: Write a function swap(a, b *int) that swaps the values at the two pointers. Call with x:=5, y:=10 and print after swapping.
